what: Yum! Brands owns KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and Habit Burger. It franchises almost all of its roughly 61,000 restaurants, so it collects a percentage of sales rather than running the restaurants itself.
customers: Franchisees who own and operate the restaurants, and through them fast-food customers in more than 155 countries.
money: the largest brand by units, mostly outside the United States
almost entirely US, with the strongest sales growth
moat: Brands people recognise everywhere, with a franchise model that earns a royalty on sales without the capital cost of owning restaurants.
risks: Debt of about $13 billion, typical of a franchised model but still large
Pizza Hut has lost share for years in several markets
Franchisee profitability determines how fast new restaurants open
Geopolitical boycotts have hurt KFC sales in some markets
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 33% and a 31% operating margin
Taco Bell keeps outgrowing the rest of US fast food
Franchising means revenue grows without the company funding new restaurants
watch: Taco Bell US same-store sales and net new restaurant openings.
